wineries.name: Vasse Felix
wineries.description: Margaret River's founding estate, where the region's first vines went in and the benchmark for its Cabernet and Chardonnay has been set ever since.
wineries.story: Perth cardiologist Dr Tom Cullity planted eight acres at Wilyabrup in 1967, acting on the scientific hunch that Margaret River could rival Bordeaux, and Vasse Felix became the region's first vineyard and winery. Now owned by the Holmes a Court family, the estate pairs one of Australia's most awarded winery restaurants with an art gallery showing works from the Holmes a Court Collection. The flagship Tom Cullity Cabernet honours the founder and is drawn largely from his original plantings.

image.alt: Vineyard rows sweeping up to the white-roofed Vasse Felix cellar door and restaurant buildings under a big sky
image.verified: downloaded 2026-07-10 from vassefelix.com.au markup, 1200x630, shows estate vineyard and cellar door complex

briefing.icebreaker: Is it true Dr Cullity used peacocks to scare the silvereyes off his first vintage?
briefing.proMove: Walk-ins are fine at the bar, but pay the extra for the $25 Icon tasting to try Tom Cullity and Heytesbury; book the upstairs restaurant well ahead for a window table over the vines.
briefing.hiddenGem: Upstairs is a wine museum and an art gallery with rotating exhibitions from the Holmes a Court Collection, free to wander before your tasting.

wineries.sommNote: The founding estate is still the region's finishing school: taste Filius against Tom Cullity and you can trace exactly how Wilyabrup Cabernet grows up.

wineries.name: Cullen Wines
wineries.description: Australia's biodynamic standard-bearer, a family estate whose Diana Madeline Cabernet blend sits among the country's greatest reds.
wineries.story: Kevin and Diana Cullen planted their Wilyabrup vineyard in 1971, and daughter Vanya Cullen has led the winemaking since 1989, converting the estate to certified biodynamics in the 2000s and making it carbon neutral. Vanya was named Halliday Wine Companion Winemaker of the Year in 2020. The two flagship wines, Diana Madeline and Kevin John, are named for her parents.

image.alt: Dawn light over dormant biodynamic vineyard rows at Cullen's Wilyabrup estate, gum trees on the horizon
image.verified: downloaded 2026-07-10 from cullenwines.com.au viticulture page, 1500x727, shows estate vineyard at sunrise

briefing.icebreaker: What actually goes into the cow-horn preparations you bury in the vineyard each autumn?
briefing.proMove: The $15 counter tasting is walk-in and redeemable against purchase; book the $45 seated tasting on OpenTable if you want Diana Madeline and Kevin John poured properly.
briefing.hiddenGem: The Spiral Garden tour walks you through the biodynamic gardens that supply the restaurant, and the estate has been certified carbon neutral since the mid-2000s.

wineries.sommNote: Taste Diana Madeline young and you will see why the Cullens never chased power: it is the quietest great Cabernet in Australia.

wineries.name: Moss Wood
wineries.description: A cult Wilyabrup estate whose Cabernet Sauvignon holds Langton's highest classification, visited strictly by appointment.
wineries.story: Bill and Sandra Pannell planted Moss Wood in 1969, making it one of Margaret River's founding vineyards, and winemaker Keith Mugford and wife Clare have owned and run it since 1985. Its estate Cabernet Sauvignon is ranked Exceptional in the Langton's Classification of Australian wine, and the unwooded Semillon has a devoted following of its own. Visits are intimate, winemaker-led affairs through the working winery and museum cellar.

image.alt: Golden-hour aerial of Moss Wood vineyard rows curving past the winery sheds and red-gravel drive
image.verified: downloaded 2026-07-10 from mosswood.com.au visit page, 1000x749, shows estate vineyard and winery buildings from the air

briefing.icebreaker: You pick the Semillon early and never oak it. When did that become the house style?
briefing.proMove: There is no walk-in cellar door: tours run by appointment (about $50 per person plus GST, max ten guests) and weekends have the most slots, so email or call weeks ahead.
briefing.hiddenGem: The tour includes barrel and tank tastings plus the museum cellar of back vintages, and the Mugfords also make a second Wilyabrup estate wine from the neighbouring Ribbon Vale vineyard.

wineries.sommNote: Moss Wood Cabernet is Wilyabrup at its most plush; cellar it a decade and it repays you with cedar and violets.

wineries.name: Woodlands
wineries.description: One of Margaret River's first five wineries, a Watson family estate pouring complimentary tastings across the road from its famous 1973 Cabernet block.
wineries.story: David and Heather Watson planted Woodlands on Caves Road at Easter 1973, and by 1982 their 'Andrew' Cabernet Sauvignon 1981 had swept trophies at the Mount Barker, Perth and Canberra shows. Sons Stuart and Andrew now run the estate, naming the reserve Cabernets after family members with each vintage. The old dry-grown vineyard sits in the heart of Wilyabrup, a stone's throw from Moss Wood and Cullen.

image.alt: The Margaret Slope vineyard at Woodlands, green rows rolling down to a dam under a clear Wilyabrup sky
image.verified: downloaded 2026-07-10 from woodlandswines.com our-story page, 1024x683, shows estate vineyard slope and dam

briefing.icebreaker: Who gets a wine named after them this year, and how does the family decide?
briefing.proMove: Seated tastings are complimentary and walk-ins work, but book ahead in school holidays; the last tasting starts at 4pm and the onsite kitchen runs to 4pm, so come hungry before then.
briefing.hiddenGem: Ask about the museum tasting: the cellar still holds back vintages of the named Cabernets, and the 1981 'Andrew' is the wine that put Woodlands on the map.

wineries.sommNote: Free tastings within sight of some of Wilyabrup's oldest Cabernet vines is the best-value hour in Margaret River.

wineries.name: Pierro
wineries.description: A quietly brilliant Wilyabrup estate whose barrel-fermented Chardonnay has held cult status among Australian collectors for four decades.
wineries.story: Physician-turned-vigneron Dr Michael Peterkin established Pierro in 1979 and planted his first vines on the Caves Road property in 1980, applying an uncompromising, science-first approach to close-planted viticulture. The estate Chardonnay quickly became one of Australia's benchmark examples and remains among the country's most sought-after whites. The L.T.C. blend's initials stand for 'a Little Touch of Chardonnay', a wink at the splash added to the Semillon Sauvignon Blanc.

image.alt: Weathered timber-post vine rows at Pierro glowing in late-afternoon light, gum trees behind
image.verified: downloaded 2026-07-10 from pierro.com.au homepage markup (Wix CDN), 1863x2436, shows estate vineyard rows at golden hour

briefing.icebreaker: The vineyard is famously close-planted for Margaret River. What did that decision cost you in the early years?
briefing.proMove: Tastings are free and walk-ins welcome, but ring ahead if you want the Chardonnay and Vintage Reserve open rather than just the L.T.C. and reds.
briefing.hiddenGem: L.T.C. officially stands for 'a Little Touch of Chardonnay', the small percentage barrel-fermented into the Semillon Sauvignon Blanc blend.

wineries.sommNote: Pierro Chardonnay is the worked, generous counterpoint to the region's leaner modern style; drink one of each and pick a side.

wines.name: Tom Cullity
wines.description: The founder's wine, drawn largely from the 1967 plantings, and Margaret River Cabernet at its most complete.
wines.sommNote: Decant an hour and serve at 17C; the Malbec lifts the florals, so do not drown it in a hot room.

wines.name: Heytesbury Chardonnay
wines.description: The estate's top Chardonnay, wild-fermented and precise, named for the Holmes a Court family company.
wines.sommNote: Give it ten minutes out of the ice bucket; the struck-match reduction blows off and the grapefruit pith arrives.

wines.name: Filius Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.description: The 'son of' Cabernet: junior Tom Cullity fruit at a weeknight price.
wines.sommNote: Serve just cool with anything char-grilled; it is the cellar door bottle to actually drink this year.

wines.name: Diana Madeline
wines.description: The biodynamic Cabernet Merlot named for the family matriarch, perennially ranked among Australia's finest reds.
wines.sommNote: Fine-boned rather than muscular; decant gently and pour it alongside food, not before.

wines.name: Kevin John Chardonnay
wines.description: Vanya Cullen's flagship Chardonnay, picked on fruit days by the biodynamic calendar and utterly singular.
wines.sommNote: Do not overchill; at 12C the ginger-curd and nougat notes open up beautifully.

wines.name: Moss Wood Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.description: The Langton's Exceptional-ranked Wilyabrup icon, plush, perfumed and built for the long haul.
wines.sommNote: If you must open one young, double-decant in the morning for dinner; better, bury it for ten years.

wines.name: Moss Wood Semillon
wines.description: Unoaked, lemongrass-fresh Semillon that has quietly built one of Margaret River's most loyal followings.
wines.sommNote: Brilliant young with shellfish, but a five-year-old bottle turns lanolin-rich and toasty without seeing a stave of oak.

wines.name: Moss Wood Chardonnay
wines.description: The estate's rich, barrel-fermented Chardonnay, a collector's counterpart to the famous Cabernet.
wines.sommNote: Generous and fig-scented; serve with richer seafood rather than delicate raw dishes.

wines.name: Margaret Cabernet Merlot Malbec
wines.description: The Watson family's reserve claret-style blend from the 1973 Woodlands vineyard, first made in 1992.
wines.sommNote: Old-vine Wilyabrup elegance in a Bordeaux shape; decant thirty minutes and serve with red meat off the grill.

wines.name: Matthew Cabernet Sauvignon
wines.description: The top of the named-Cabernet series, a museum-released pure Cabernet from the old dry-grown block.
wines.sommNote: Released with bottle age already on it; open an hour ahead and let the cigar-box perfume do the talking.

wines.name: Wilyabrup Valley Cabernet Sauvignon Merlot
wines.description: The estate's everyday claret, an honest window onto the same Wilyabrup dirt as the named Cabernets.
wines.sommNote: The smart buy at the free tasting; drinks well now with a light chill in summer.

wines.name: Pierro Chardonnay
wines.description: The cult barrel-fermented Chardonnay that made Pierro's name and helped define the richer Margaret River style.
wines.sommNote: Full-throttle and creamy; serve at cellar temperature with equally generous food and it sings.

wines.name: L.T.C. Semillon Sauvignon Blanc
wines.description: Margaret River's classic white blend with 'a Little Touch of Chardonnay' folded in for texture.
wines.sommNote: The thinking drinker's SSB: the chardonnay splash rounds the acid, so pour it with food rather than as an aperitif.
